comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude authorized text from the unpublished-line substring scan**

When an unpublished line is a substring of a longer published line, subtracting `texts_ok` only removes exact matches, so the substring scan rejects legitimate published content. This already affects the checked-in data: posting p002's default version publishes diary2 block 2 line 1, which contains the shorter reading from unpublished block 4 line 1. Even with the unpublished block correctly emptied and all gates satisfied, `leak_check` reports a leak and posting exits 3; `--force` cannot override it. Exempt occurrences within authorized published readings (while retaining the structural check on unpublished blocks) so overlapping wording does not prevent publication.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the complete origin hostname instead of a URL substring**

If the supplied clone's origin is `https://notgithub.com/4444J99/versforms.git` or `https://example.invalid/github.com/4444J99/versforms.git`, this function returns true because the regex matches anywhere in the URL. The remaining repository checks only establish that the clone is clean and level with its own origin, so they cannot catch this mistaken identity. Consequently, `fill_public_repo` can replace `site/` and commit in an unintended repository despite the identity hard stop reporting PASS. Parse the URL and SCP-style SSH forms and require the hostname to equal `github.com` and the repository path to match exactly.
